trial_court: Additional District Judge, Delhi, HMA No. 427 of 2000
facts_of_case: The respondent filed a petition for divorce on the ground of cruelty under Sections 13(1)(ia) and 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The petitioner did not appear in court and the petition was dismissed in default. A counter-claim for divorce was also inadvertently dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: A party who remains absent on the date of listing without any reasonable excuse cannot claim that he was not aware of the proceedings.
legal_principles.held: Despite being aware of the dismissal of the Section 9 petition, the appellant made no efforts to have the said application restored.

legal_principles.principle: A party's counsel should check the next date and know about the fate of a petition.
legal_principles.held: The Counsel ought to have checked the next date and known about the fate of the petition.

legal_principles.principle: A party's conduct in the past can be considered while deciding a case.
legal_principles.held: The conduct of the appellant in the past should disentitle him to relief in this appeal.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to honour orders can be considered while deciding a case.
legal_principles.held: The appellant has also not been honouring the orders for payment of maintenance and, therefore, the present proceedings would result in further harassment to the respondent.

outcome.final_order: Divorce granted to the respondent by ex parte judgment on 12.10.2001, which is set aside and a fresh decree of divorce is passed in favour of the respondent.

keywords: Latin maxim: Actio non favet inuria
use_for_drafting: representing clients in restitution of conjugal rights cases
